title: Choose and show a strategy
subject: RSHE
outcome: Show a coping strategy in a real situation.
credit: Lesson resource · CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: free for classroom use, share and adapt with credit, no resale
source_note: Current date, period and exact row69 outcome supplied in the owner's Week6 brief. Six-outcome grid cross-checked against accepted Week1 lesson source, with Week2 outcome and strategy choices read directly from its accepted ZIP and Weeks3–5 from accepted packs. The underlying workbook was not reopened in this return. Parenthetical labels appear only inside the relevant verbatim outcomes; no named campaign resource is reproduced.

outcomes.outcome: Recognise that change can feel hard (Children's MH Week).
Name a big feeling and a way to manage it.
Talk about a worry with a trusted adult (Time to Talk).
Identify who helps me through change.
Show a coping strategy in a real situation.

strategies.label: Soft breath
steps: Sit or stand in your safe, usual way.
Take a soft breath in.
Let a soft breath out at your own pace.
Stop or ask for help if it does not feel good.
strategies.staff: Only the familiar school-agreed comfortable breathing routine. No holding, forced depth, phase counts, prescribed rate, eyes-closed demand or timer pacing. Stop/change if uncomfortable.

strategies.label: Look and count
steps: Look at three things you can see.
Notice two safe touch points, like feet and a seat.
Notice one sound in the quiet room.
Stop or choose another card if you wish.
strategies.staff: Retain Week3 familiar authored3–2–1 noticing routine and usual sensory access. No added noise, taste, smell, unfamiliar objects or touching someone. If any part is unsuitable, choose another familiar strategy or agreed adaptation.

strategies.label: Small hand move
steps: Sit in your safe, usual way.
Rest your hands where they feel fine.
Open softly. Close softly. Let them rest.
Stop or choose another card if you wish.
strategies.staff: Use familiar agreed small movement and existing physical/sensory adaptations. No force, tight grip, stretch/range target or physical performance grade.

strategies.label: Ask a trusted adult
steps: Choose a trusted adult role for the story.
Use words, a help card or your usual aid.
Ask for help with the next step.
If the adult is busy, try another trusted adult.
strategies.staff: Known trusted school role and usual safe route only. TA responds to the actual selected request; words may be voiced exactly as chosen through agreed access. This is not a personal disclosure. Do not infer independent spoken speech from TA voicing.

strategies.label: Ask for agreed quiet space
steps: Use a help card, words or your usual aid.
Ask the adult for the agreed quiet space.
Use the space with the agreed adult support.
Return with help when ready.
strategies.staff: Only the already agreed supervised pause/quiet-place route. Do not send learner away alone, imply secrecy or remove usual supervision. It is valid to show the request while TA confirms next step; do not invent actual space use if it was not observed.

stations.title: A change of plan
stations.scene: A pupil thought the class would draw first. The new plan is to tidy first, then draw. The pupil says, 'I feel cross.'
stations.practical: In a calm, pre-explained activity, show two plain cards for tidy and draw. Learner may show an agreed familiar strategy, then place/point to the new order if they wish. No surprise actual plan switch or induced disappointment.
stations.example: The story pupil picks small hand move, shows the soft steps in their usual safe position, then points to tidy first.
stations.question: Who could help? Which strategy could fit?

stations.title: A noisy room story
stations.scene: Lots of people talk in a room. A pupil wants a calm moment.
stations.practical: Read/show the story in the ordinary quiet room; no sound playback or raised voices. Learner may enact a familiar routine or use their normal mode to request the agreed supported quiet-space/help route. TA acknowledges and follows usual supervision. The story noise is never created.
stations.example: The story pupil selects the quiet-space help card and shows it to the TA. The TA confirms the agreed supported route. Record whether the request only or actual supported use was observed.
stations.question: Which safe step could the pupil show?

stations.title: A task feels hard
stations.scene: A pupil looks at a new task. They say, 'I am not sure how to start.'
stations.practical: Offer a very short familiar task such as placing two plain cards in a row, already explained and optional. Do not set a genuinely difficult/frustrating task. Learner can ask TA for first-step help or show another familiar coping step in ordinary calm conditions.
stations.example: The story pupil chooses a teacher/TA role, selects Can you show the first step? with their usual aid, and the TA models one card only. Record actual request and support.
stations.question: Who could help and how? What strategy could fit?

circuit_rule: A short practical scenario circuit in a calm room. The contexts are invented and mild; the chosen safe strategy action is actually shown. No added noise, surprise changes, frustration test, demanded big feeling or real personal worry. One familiar strategy may fit all three; no requirement to use all strategies, finish all stations or stay if uncomfortable. Pass, stop, observer role and supported return are valid. Use up to three short private opportunities with the TA; record fewer if needed, never rush or invent completion. Other pupils revisit neutral strategy cards/book plans.
real_situation_rule: Keep the exact outcome. Record structured classroom simulation separately from a naturally arising real situation or a specific dated prior observation. Actual strategy steps shown in the circuit are evidence of a demonstration in that context; they do not by themselves prove spontaneous real-life coping or meet the real-situation element. For row69, comment clearly when only simulation was seen and leave real-situation use not yet observed. If a naturally arising safe relevant classroom situation or prior dated record supplies evidence, note context/date and actual observed use without inducing distress or requesting personal disclosure. Real situations can be ordinary and calm; being upset is never a requirement.
show_rule: A selected card, explanation, copied plan or intention alone does not show a strategy. Observe actual familiar routine steps, a real selected help request through usual mode with TA response, or agreed supported pause use as applicable. Record precisely what happened, including a request without actual space use. If no action is seen, record not observed. An exact adult scribe/voicing can convey the learner's chosen message; it cannot substitute for physical routine action or prove independent spoken speech.
independence: Keep word bank, sentence starter, visible model, strategy/help cards and usual aids for all routes. For Week3 independent-use evidence, after general task cue the learner selects, starts and follows a familiar calming routine without adult next-step content prompts. Reading/communication/physical access and visual cue stay; log any content prompts separately. Prompted practice is valid teaching/evidence at that support level, not independent use.
privacy_pupil: Use the made-up stories in class. For real help, ask a trusted adult in private. You can stop, pass or ask for help.

private_card.title: My strategy that works
private_card.subtitle: A card to help me choose next time
private_card.instruction: Keep this card. Write, draw, point or ask for a scribe if you wish.
private_card.note: All answers are fine. Leave a space blank if you wish. The title does not mean a strategy must work each time. No worry, private story or adult name goes on this card. You do not have to show it to the group.

safeguarding: If a pupil cannot identify a trusted adult or safe support, support privately and do not press. Offer a familiar school role and help make contact through the school route; accept a blank card or pass. Any disclosure goes to the safeguarding lead through school procedure. Listen calmly, reassure, do not probe or promise secrecy. Follow urgent school procedures where needed. Do not write disclosure details in this pack, a pupil card, book task or shared learning evidence. Private pupil cards are not collected, photographed or displayed for assessment. Staff support a card only with pupil agreement; pupil keeps it.
support_route: Use known trusted adults and the already agreed supervised help/quiet-space route. If first adult is busy or help does not fit, support asking another trusted adult. Do not approach an unfamiliar adult alone or leave supervision. No pupil must endorse a specific person or name real supports.

routes.Supported: Model one familiar strategy first, offer two safe choices and return the action/choice to the pupil. Keep all aids; prompt as needed and record cues accurately. Respect stop/pass. Reduced station count is valid.
routes.Independent: Keep all aids and normal access. After general cue, learner chooses and actually shows a familiar safe strategy; record any adult next-step content prompts. Apply Week3 independence only to actual unprompted calming routine use, not to copied plans or TA-led steps.
routes.Aspire: Keep all aids. Show a suitable strategy and suggest another safe option if unhelpful, or explain what help the story pupil could ask for. No extra station, writing, personal account or demand to feel calm is required.

success: Show the chosen steps in the usual safe way.
Show or choose a next safe step if needed.
timing: 0–3 calm story starter; 3–7 recall familiar choices; 7–11 model actual use and check; 11–12 reset.
12–17 preview/practise three mild stations; 17–20 private hinge; 20–24 choose and plan one starting strategy; 24–25 reset.
25–34 short private circuit opportunities with TA; 34–37 own helpfulness/card and one next step/response; 37–40 private exit and adult grid update. Prior evidence references prepared before lesson.

scaffolds.model: The story pupil could try a small hand move.
They show a small hand move: open softly, close softly, rest.
For the noisy-room story they could ask for agreed quiet space.
We need to see the chosen safe steps, not just a card choice.

scaffolds.start: In the story, they will try ... .
scaffolds.model: In the story, they will try soft breath at their own pace.
They showed a hand move. The help tick is their own choice.

scaffolds.start: A next safe step could be ... .
scaffolds.model: A next safe step could be to ask a trusted adult.

hinge.question: What shows that a strategy was used?
hinge.A: Only point to a card, with no strategy step shown.
hinge.B: Show the chosen safe steps, or make the chosen help request.
hinge.decision: Check privately via usual words/pointing/aid. If B or clear equivalent, proceed. If A, unclear/no response, re-model card-choice versus actual action, then use parallel check. A pass is not misunderstanding. The selected help request must actually be communicated; merely saying what the story pupil might do is a plan.

parallel.question: A pupil chooses a hand-move card but does no move. What was seen?
parallel.A: A choice only. The move has not been shown.
parallel.B: Proof that they used the hand move.

misconceptions: Choosing or describing a strategy proves it was used independently or works.
Observe the actual action/request and record access and prompts. Own helpfulness report is separate. Yes/A bit/No/Not sure are all valid, with no guarantee of calming.
The pupil must be upset, finish every station or share a real worry for assessment.

Use ordinary calm, invented mild contexts. No induced distress, noise or frustration. Pass, stop and fewer stations are valid. Record exact context and no observation honestly; real-life use is not inferred from simulation.

adaptations.Cognition & Learning: Explicit short modelling, strategy steps visible, small card set and two-choice support. Repeat only one familiar routine if useful. Fade adult answer/step cues while retaining all aids.
adaptations.Communication & Interaction: Wait time, familiar aid, pointing, exact voicing/scribe and readback for choices/reflection. Actual physical routine cannot be scribed. No demand for speech or eye contact.
adaptations.SEMH: Predictable mild story-only circuit, pre-explained order, no emotional trigger questions or public performance. Pass/stop/observer role, quiet pause and supported return; never require upset before practice.
adaptations.Sensory/Physical: Ordinary quiet room, usual safe position and agreed aids. No added noise or forced movement/breath pattern. Choose an alternative familiar strategy if a sensation/action does not suit.
adaptations.EAL: Plan in any language. Explain strategy, show, help and change with short examples. Usual language support can convey the pupil's own choices; record exact support.

cold_call_label: Optional private fictional check prompts; never public personal questions.

cold_call.F: Which familiar safe card could fit this story?
cold_call.M: What did the story pupil actually show?
cold_call.H: What else could they try if it did not help?

ta_focus.I_do: Model a familiar actual strategy step and distinguish a card choice from use. State that no one has to be upset. Check privately with all aids.
ta_focus.We_do: Read/preview the three calm stations without creating noise or frustration. Rehearse supported steps, mark as teaching, and keep bank/starter/model.
ta_focus.Independent: Observe the learner's actual action/request, mode, access and content prompts. Accept stop/pass; context is structured unless a genuine natural situation is recorded. Update six-outcome grid from specific evidence only.

prompt_ladder: Point to the place or instruction.
Model the first step only, then return the task.
grid_rule: Six verbatim outcomes, initially unticked, with tick choices for Shown / With help / Not seen and a comment field for date, context, what was actually seen, access/prompts and source of earlier evidence. Do not tick all six from one performance. Prior evidence must be a specific dated record, never invented. Week3 independent requirement and Week6 real-situation requirement need explicit evidence in their comments; if absent, mark Not seen for that requirement and describe supported/simulation progress. A pass is not failure. No personal worry, private card contents or names.
observation_record: One adult circuit record with three station entries A/B/C: date, structured/naturally arising/prior context, chosen familiar strategy, actual action/request seen or not seen, usual access, adult content prompts, shown with aids/no next-step cues / shown with content cues / not observed, stop/pass, own helpfulness if freely offered, next opportunity. Keep identity blank/generic for local staff record; no name in published pack. Do not equate observed quiet-space request with actual space use or adult-voiced choice with independent speech.
evidence: Evidence Sheet includes half-term six-outcome tick/comment grid and actual TA observation record, plus book-first pupil guide. Use actual strategy action/request and exact context/support, optional own helpfulness, one NS and own response. Private strategy card is kept, not collected. No inference of all outcomes, clinical benefit or real-life generalisation. Weekly Plan Row explicitly notes assessing week.
marking: VF verbal feedback; WS worked with support; I independent; NS next step in green; // self-edit; ? read this back to me; E actual evidence banked; R responded. R only when Voice and Audience are present, one NS is set and the pupil responds in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. Offer to the Communication portfolio; staff confirm mapping.
where_this_leads: This helps me use a safe step or ask for help with a new task or job.
hold: BUILD RSHE Spring1 ends after this week. LAUNCH RSE Spring1 Weeks1–3 await full brief after acceptance. Weeks4–5 held for owner decision; nothing built.

paragraphs: Choose and show a strategy
Show a coping strategy in a real situation.
Use the made-up stories in class. For real help, ask a trusted adult in private. You can stop, pass or ask for help.
Your try
Pick a safe step you know. Show the steps in your usual safe way. You can use your card and aids. An adult can help. They will note the help they give. No one has to feel upset to try.
A model
The story pupil picks small hand move. They open softly, close softly and rest. A card choice on its own does not show the move.
Show and own check
Words: try, stop, help, sure
Start: They showed ... . My check is ... .
Model: They showed a hand move. The help tick is their own choice.
Your own check
Did it help? Yes · A bit · No · Not sure. All four are fine. The choice is yours. You can point or ask for a scribe. No one can fill it from a guess.
A card to keep
Use My strategy that works if you wish. You do not have to fill it or show it to the group. Its title does not mean a step must work each time. No real worry or name goes on it.
Your next step
Keep your first try. Use one next step. Reply in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. You can stop, pass, watch or come back with help.
Six outcome check

Staff page. Use work codes, not names. Start with all boxes blank. Tick one state for each row only when the work supports it. Add date, context, what was seen, aids, cues and source. Do not fill all six from one try.
Week 3: keep normal aids. To tick its own-use aim, see a calm step used with no adult next-step cues. If only helped use was seen, mark this aim Not seen and note the helped progress.

Week 6: a planned story try is not proof of real use. Mark the real-use aim Not seen unless a safe real event or dated prior work shows it. Note the date, context, acts and help. Do not cause upset to get proof.
A pass is not failure. No real worries, private card details or names here. Keep real concerns in the school’s own safe record.
TA circuit work note
Use a work code, not a name. Context: S planned story try; N safe real event that came up; P dated prior work. Log what was seen, not what was hoped. The class try is S unless a real event is clear.

No trusted adult to choose? Give private help; do not press. Any real disclosure goes to the safeguarding lead through school route. Listen; give calm support. Do not probe or promise a secret. paragraphs: Staff answers and teaching notes
Outcome and boundaries

Show a coping strategy in a real situation. A short practical scenario circuit in a calm room. The contexts are invented and mild; the chosen safe strategy action is actually shown. No added noise, surprise changes, frustration test, demanded big feeling or real personal worry. One familiar strategy may fit all three; no requirement to use all strategies, finish all stations or stay if uncomfortable. Pass, stop, observer role and supported return are valid. Use up to three short private opportunities with the TA; record fewer if needed, never rush or invent completion. Other pupils revisit neutral strategy cards/book plans.
Familiar choices

Soft breath; look and count; small hand move; ask a trusted adult; ask for agreed quiet space. Use only already familiar school-agreed versions and established access. This is an assessing week, not the introduction of a new coping protocol.
Soft breath
Only the familiar school-agreed comfortable breathing routine. No holding, forced depth, phase counts, prescribed rate, eyes-closed demand or timer pacing. Stop/change if uncomfortable.
Look and count

Retain Week 3 familiar, authored 3–2–1 noticing routine and usual sensory access. No added noise, taste, smell, unfamiliar objects or touching someone. If any part is unsuitable, choose another familiar strategy or agreed adaptation.
Small hand move
Use familiar agreed small movement and existing physical/sensory adaptations. No force, tight grip, stretch/range target or physical performance grade.
Ask a trusted adult

Known trusted school role and usual safe route only. TA responds to the actual selected request; words may be voiced exactly as chosen through agreed access. This is not a personal disclosure. Do not infer independent spoken speech from TA voicing.
Ask for agreed quiet space

Only the already agreed supervised pause/quiet-place route. Do not send learner away alone, imply secrecy or remove usual supervision. It is valid to show the request while TA confirms next step; do not invent actual space use if it was not observed.
Actual use

A selected card, explanation, copied plan or intention alone does not show a strategy. Observe actual familiar routine steps, a real selected help request through usual mode with TA response, or agreed supported pause use as applicable. Record precisely what happened, including a request without actual space use. If no action is seen, record not observed. An exact adult scribe/voicing can convey the learner's chosen message; it cannot substitute for physical routine action or prove independent spoken speech.
Stations and checks
A A change of plan

A pupil thought the class would draw first. The new plan is to tidy first, then draw. The pupil says, 'I feel cross.' In a calm, pre-explained activity, show two plain cards for tidy and draw. Learner may show an agreed familiar strategy, then place/point to the new order if they wish. No surprise actual plan switch or induced disappointment. Example: The story pupil picks small hand move, shows the soft steps in their usual safe position, then points to tidy first.
B A noisy room story

Lots of people talk in a room. A pupil wants a calm moment. Read/show the story in the ordinary quiet room; no sound playback or raised voices. Learner may enact a familiar routine or use their normal mode to request the agreed supported quiet-space/help route. TA acknowledges and follows usual supervision. The story noise is never created. Example: The story pupil selects the quiet-space help card and shows it to the TA. The TA confirms the agreed supported route. Record whether the request only or actual supported use was observed.
C A task feels hard

A pupil looks at a new task. They say, 'I am not sure how to start.' Offer a very short familiar task such as placing two plain cards in a row, already explained and optional. Do not set a genuinely difficult/frustrating task. Learner can ask TA for first-step help or show another familiar coping step in ordinary calm conditions. Example: The story pupil chooses a teacher/TA role, selects Can you show the first step? with their usual aid, and the TA models one card only. Record actual request and support.
Model check

Choice or explanation alone is not actual use. A routine action or chosen help request must actually be shown. Record supported request versus actual quiet-space use precisely. TA voicing preserves the learner’s chosen words; it does not show independent speech.
Main and parallel hinge

Main B: show the steps or make the selected request. A only points to a card. Re-model choice versus use if needed. Parallel A: card selected with no hand move is choice only. B wrongly claims use. Check privately through usual aid; pass remains unobserved.
Misconceptions

Choosing or describing a strategy proves it was used independently or works. Observe the actual action/request and record access and prompts. Own helpfulness report is separate. Yes/A bit/No/Not sure are all valid, with no guarantee of calming.

The pupil must be upset, finish every station or share a real worry for assessment. Use ordinary calm, invented mild contexts. No induced distress, noise or frustration. Pass, stop and fewer stations are valid. Record exact context and no observation honestly; real-life use is not inferred from simulation.
Assessment and private support
Six outcome grid

Six verbatim outcomes, initially unticked, with tick choices for Shown / With help / Not seen and a comment field for date, context, what was actually seen, access/prompts and source of earlier evidence. Do not tick all six from one performance. Prior evidence must be a specific dated record, never invented. Week3 independent requirement and Week6 real-situation requirement need explicit evidence in their comments; if absent, mark Not seen for that requirement and describe supported/simulation progress. A pass is not failure. No personal worry, private card contents or names.
Real situation requirement

Keep the exact outcome. Record structured classroom simulation separately from a naturally arising real situation or a specific dated prior observation. Actual strategy steps shown in the circuit are evidence of a demonstration in that context; they do not by themselves prove spontaneous real-life coping or meet the real-situation element. For row69, comment clearly when only simulation was seen and leave real-situation use not yet observed. If a naturally arising safe relevant classroom situation or prior dated record supplies evidence, note context/date and actual observed use without inducing distress or requesting personal disclosure. Real situations can be ordinary and calm; being upset is never a requirement.
Independent calming use

Keep word bank, sentence starter, visible model, strategy/help cards and usual aids for all routes. For Week3 independent-use evidence, after general task cue the learner selects, starts and follows a familiar calming routine without adult next-step content prompts. Reading/communication/physical access and visual cue stay; log any content prompts separately. Prompted practice is valid teaching/evidence at that support level, not independent use.
Records and private support
Evidence record

One adult circuit record with three station entries A/B/C: date, structured/naturally arising/prior context, chosen familiar strategy, actual action/request seen or not seen, usual access, adult content prompts, shown with aids/no next-step cues / shown with content cues / not observed, stop/pass, own helpfulness if freely offered, next opportunity. Keep identity blank/generic for local staff record; no name in published pack. Do not equate observed quiet-space request with actual space use or adult-voiced choice with independent speech.
Own helpfulness

Yes / A bit / No / Not sure are equally valid. Leave all choices blank until the learner chooses. A scribe marks only an exact selected response and reads it back. No positive adult assumption or requirement to calm down.
Private card and safeguarding

If a pupil cannot identify a trusted adult or safe support, support privately and do not press. Offer a familiar school role and help make contact through the school route; accept a blank card or pass. Any disclosure goes to the safeguarding lead through school procedure. Listen calmly, reassure, do not probe or promise secrecy. Follow urgent school procedures where needed. Do not write disclosure details in this pack, a pupil card, book task or shared learning evidence. Private pupil cards are not collected, photographed or displayed for assessment. Staff support a card only with pupil agreement; pupil keeps it.
Feedback and marking

VF verbal feedback; WS worked with support; I independent; NS next step in green; // self-edit; ? read this back to me; E actual evidence banked; R responded. R only when Voice and Audience are present, one NS is set and the pupil responds in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. Offer to the Communication portfolio; staff confirm mapping.
Scope

Only BUILD Spring 1 Week 6 authored. Assessing week, Wednesday 10 February 2027 P1, Year A. Six-outcome parenthetical labels occur only in exact outcome rows; no separate named campaign resources. No later strand built.
Familiar safe steps
Use steps you know. Keep your usual aids. No one has to feel upset. Stop or choose a new card if a step does not suit you.
Soft breath
1. Sit or stand in your safe, usual way.
2. Take a soft breath in.
3. Let a soft breath out at your own pace.
4. Stop or ask for help if it does not feel good.
Look and count
1. Look at three things you can see.
2. Notice two safe touch points, like feet and a seat.
3. Notice one sound in the quiet room.
4. Stop or choose another card if you wish.
Small hand move
1. Sit in your safe, usual way.
2. Rest your hands where they feel fine.
3. Open softly. Close softly. Let them rest.
4. Stop or choose another card if you wish.
Soft breath: no hold, no force, your own pace. Look and count: use the quiet room and safe touch points. Hand move: no tight grip or force.
Ask for safe help
Ask a trusted adult
1. Choose a trusted adult role for the story.
2. Use words, a help card or your usual aid.
3. Ask for help with the next step.
4. If the adult is busy, try another trusted adult.
Ask for agreed quiet space
1. Use a help card, words or your usual aid.
2. Ask the adult for the agreed quiet space.
3. Use the space with the agreed adult support.
4. Return with help when ready.
Safe route
Use an adult you know and trust. Use the help or quiet-space route agreed at school. Stay with the agreed adult support. Do not go off alone to a new adult or place.
A request is a step
Use the card, words or your usual aid to make your chosen request. The adult can voice the words you pick. Saying what a story pupil might do is a plan; show your chosen request to the adult.
Use the made-up stories in class. For real help, ask a trusted adult in private. You can stop, pass or ask for help.
Three mild story stations
All stories are made up. The room stays calm and quiet. You can try one safe step you know. You do not have to finish all three.
A A change of plan
A pupil thought the class would draw first. The new plan is to tidy first, then draw. The pupil says, 'I feel cross.'
Who could help? Which strategy could fit?
B A noisy room story
Lots of people talk in a room. A pupil wants a calm moment.
Which safe step could the pupil show?
C A task feels hard
A pupil looks at a new task. They say, 'I am not sure how to start.'
Who could help and how? What strategy could fit?
Your choice
Pick a familiar card. Show its safe steps or make the chosen help request. Your words, model and usual aids stay. You can use one safe step for more than one story.
No loud noise, surprise change or hard task will be made. You can stop, pass, watch or come back with help.
My strategy that works
A card to help me choose next time
Keep this card. Write, draw, point or ask for a scribe if you wish.
Today I tried
A next safe step
Did it help?
A next choice

All answers are fine. Any space can stay blank. The title does not mean a step must work each time. No real worry, private story or adult name goes here. You do not have to show this card to the group. Keep it.
Aids for the story tasks
Keep words, start and model in view. Your usual aids stay.
Story starter
Words: pupil, change, cross, help
Start: The story pupil could try ... .
Model: The story pupil could try a small hand move.
Model check
Words: choose, show, step, help
Start: They show the step by ... .
Model: They show a small hand move: open softly, close softly, rest.
Guided circuit practice
Words: breath, move, help, space
Start: For story ... they could ... .
Model: For the noisy-room story they could ask for agreed quiet space.
Private hinge
Words: card, show, try, help
Start: We need to see ... .
Model: We need to see the chosen safe steps, not just a card choice.
Use the stories in class. You can point, use an aid or pass. To show a physical step, do the safe action; a scribe cannot do it for you.
Aids for your safe try
Choose and plan
Words: choose, step, stop, adult
Start: In the story, they will try ... .
Model: In the story, they will try soft breath at their own pace.
Show and own check
Words: try, stop, help, sure
Start: They showed ... . My check is ... .
Model: They showed a hand move. The help tick is their own choice.
Feedback and exit
Words: next, help, adult, card
Start: A next safe step could be ... .
Model: A next safe step could be to ask a trusted adult.
Your next step
Keep your first try. Use one next step. Reply in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode.
Help in private
For real help, ask a trusted adult in private. Use your known school route and agreed adult support. If one adult is busy, ask another trusted adult. You can stop, pass or come back with help.
No real worries or names in class work. Your keep card stays with you. You do not have to say a step helped.
Words for a safe strategy
Use words with the familiar cards. Point, say or use an aid.
A model
The story pupil picks a small hand move, then opens softly, closes softly and rests. The action was shown.
Your own check
Did it help? Yes · A bit · No · Not sure. All are fine. No one can choose for you.
Help
You can stop or pass. For real help, ask a trusted adult in private. Use your usual safe route.

paragraphs: Teacher and cover planner
Choose and show a strategy
Wednesday 10 February 2027 · P1 · 40 minutes · Year A
BUILD · three to four learners · Spring 1 Week 6 · assessing week
Theme Resilience & Change. Six-week term; final week.
Thread tags: SMSC S/So (M/C none); British Values IL/MR (D/RL/T none).
Exact outcome
Show a coping strategy in a real situation.
Source: owner brief, BUILD Weekly Spring row 69. The six outcomes are checked against accepted lesson packs. The workbook was not reopened; no independent cell check is claimed.
What this lesson assesses

Observe actual familiar strategy steps or a selected help request in three mild practical contexts. Choice or explanation alone is not shown use. The circuit is structured classroom practice. Do not infer spontaneous or generalised real-life coping; the real-situation element requires specific naturally arising or dated prior evidence. Being upset is never required.
Prepare

Prepare dated prior evidence references before teaching. Have books, familiar strategy cards, two plain tidy/draw cards, two plain task cards, usual aids and agreed supervised help/pause route. Support Cards pages 1–2 give five familiar options; page 3 gives the station stories; page 4 is the pupil keep card; pages 5–6 hold seven aid sets. Evidence Sheet has pupil guide, six-outcome grid and TA circuit record.
Where this leads
This helps me use a safe step or ask for help with a new task or job.
Forty minute sequence
12/13/15-minute chunks; two one-minute resets are inside forty minutes. Offer up to three short opportunities. Fewer stations, pass, stop or observer role are valid. Do not rush the small group.
Teaching and response routes
Chunk 1

0–3: read the calm change-of-plan story. 3–7: recall the five familiar school-agreed strategies. 7–11: model one actual routine or help request and distinguish it from merely picking a card. Check privately in usual mode. No one has to feel upset. 11–12: quiet reset.
Chunk 2

12–17: preview the three mild contexts and practise supported steps. Explain the circuit order in advance. The noisy-room story stays in an ordinary quiet room. No surprise plan change, loud noise or hard task is created. 17–20: main hinge B, then parallel A if needed. 20–24: choose and plan one starting strategy with aids. 24–25: quiet reset.
Chunk 3

25–34: TA offers private short station opportunities. Other pupils use neutral cards/book plans. Record actions, exact context, aids and content prompts. Stop or reduce opportunities as needed. 34–37: pupil gives their own optional helpfulness check, keeps the card and responds to one next step. 37–40: private exit and specific adult grid update; finish records using prepared prior references.
Supported

Model one familiar strategy first, offer two safe choices and return the action/choice to the pupil. Keep all aids; prompt as needed and record cues accurately. Respect stop/pass. Reduced station count is valid.
Independent

Keep all aids and normal access. After general cue, learner chooses and actually shows a familiar safe strategy; record any adult next-step content prompts. Apply Week3 independence only to actual unprompted calming routine use, not to copied plans or TA-led steps.
Aspire

Keep all aids. Show a suitable strategy and suggest another safe option if unhelpful, or explain what help the story pupil could ask for. No extra station, writing, personal account or demand to feel calm is required.
Worked example and fade

Model a small hand move in the usual safe position: open softly, close softly, rest. Keep the step card and model visible. Offer two familiar choices for supported practice. For a later observed try give a general cue and fade next-step content cues only. Normal aids stay. Prompted teaching and later action are recorded separately.
TA focus

I do: show an actual step; state no upset is needed. We do: preview without noise or frustration and mark rehearsal as teaching. Independent: log actual use/request, context, mode, aids and cues. Pass is valid. Use only specific evidence for the grid.
Aids for each task
All routes retain each bank, starter and visible model, strategy card and usual aids. These seven sets also appear on Support Cards pages 5–6.
Story starter
Words: pupil, change, cross, help
Start: The story pupil could try ... .
Model: The story pupil could try a small hand move.
Model check
Words: choose, show, step, help
Start: They show the step by ... .
Model: They show a small hand move: open softly, close softly, rest.
Guided circuit practice
Words: breath, move, help, space
Start: For story ... they could ... .
Model: For the noisy-room story they could ask for agreed quiet space.
Private hinge
Words: card, show, try, help
Start: We need to see ... .
Model: We need to see the chosen safe steps, not just a card choice.
Choose and plan
Words: choose, step, stop, adult
Start: In the story, they will try ... .
Model: In the story, they will try soft breath at their own pace.
Show and own check
Words: try, stop, help, sure
Start: They showed ... . My check is ... .
Model: They showed a hand move. The help tick is their own choice.
Feedback and exit
Words: next, help, adult, card
Start: A next safe step could be ... .
Model: A next safe step could be to ask a trusted adult.
Prompt ladder

1 Point to the place or instruction. 2 Ask a short question privately. 3 Rephrase. 4 Provide a scaffold or choice. 5 Model the first step only, then return the task. Allow processing time. Separate normal access from adult next-step content cues in the record.
Checks and planned access
Success criteria
Choose a safe familiar strategy.
Show the chosen steps in the usual safe way.
Show or choose a next safe step if needed.
Check after the model

Ask what was actually shown. Pointing to a strategy card is a choice. A visible familiar routine, or a chosen help request actually conveyed to the TA, shows use in that context. A scribe can preserve chosen words or feedback but cannot perform a physical routine for the learner.
Main hinge and decision rule

B fits: show chosen safe steps or make the selected help request. A only points to a card. Check privately through usual access. If A or unclear, re-model choice versus action and use the parallel. A pass is not misunderstanding.
Parallel hinge
A fits: choosing a hand-move card without moving shows a choice only. B wrongly claims use. Recheck privately with aids; keep unsupported claims out of the record.
Cognition and Learning
Explicit short modelling, strategy steps visible, small card set and two-choice support. Repeat only one familiar routine if useful. Fade adult answer/step cues while retaining all aids.
Communication and Interaction
Wait time, familiar aid, pointing, exact voicing/scribe and readback for choices/reflection. Actual physical routine cannot be scribed. No demand for speech or eye contact.
SEMH

Predictable mild story-only circuit, pre-explained order, no emotional trigger questions or public performance. Pass/stop/observer role, quiet pause and supported return; never require upset before practice.
Sensory/Physical
Ordinary quiet room, usual safe position and agreed aids. No added noise or forced movement/breath pattern. Choose an alternative familiar strategy if a sensation/action does not suit.
EAL
Plan in any language. Explain strategy, show, help and change with short examples. Usual language support can convey the pupil's own choices; record exact support.
Optional private story checks
F: Which familiar safe card could fit this story? M: What did the story pupil actually show? H: What else could they try if it did not help? Use only fictional checks; pointing and pass remain valid.
Misconceptions

Choosing or describing a step is not actual use, independence or proof it helped. A pupil need not be upset, complete all stations or share a real worry. Record actual actions, support, own feedback and observation gaps honestly.
Evidence and private support
Six outcome grid

Evidence Sheet page 2 has six verbatim outcomes, initially unticked, with Shown / With help / Not seen and comment fields. Use specific dated work and source references. Do not tick all six from one performance. Week 3 independence needs actual calming-routine use without next-step content cues, with normal aids retained. If absent, mark that requirement Not seen and describe supported progress.
Real situation requirement

The circuit is a structured simulation. Its actual actions show demonstration in that context only. For Week 6, leave real-situation use Not seen unless a naturally arising safe relevant classroom situation or specific dated prior record shows actual use. Note date, context, observed action and support. Never create distress or seek a personal worry to obtain evidence. Ordinary calm real situations are valid.
TA observation and own feedback

Evidence Sheet pages 3–4 separate station A/B/C, context/date, chosen strategy, actual action/request, mode/aids, adult content cues, status and next opportunity. A request for space does not prove space use. Exact TA voicing is access, not independent speech. The pupil’s Yes / A bit / No / Not sure is optional and distinct from observed use. No positive tick is prefilled.
Safe routines and supervision

Use only familiar school-agreed options with existing adaptations. Soft breath has no hold, forced depth/rate or timer pace. Look/count uses ordinary quiet surroundings and safe contact points; no added noise, unfamiliar objects or touching another person. Hand move has no force or range target. Help/space uses known trusted adults and the already agreed supervised route. Stop/change if uncomfortable.
Safeguarding and pupil card

If a pupil cannot identify a trusted adult or safe support, support privately and do not press. Offer a familiar school role and help make contact through the school route; accept a blank card or pass. Any disclosure goes to the safeguarding lead through school procedure. Listen calmly, reassure, do not probe or promise secrecy. Follow urgent school procedures where needed. Do not write disclosure details in this pack, a pupil card, book task or shared learning evidence. Private pupil cards are not collected, photographed or displayed for assessment. Staff support a card only with pupil agreement; pupil keeps it.
Feedback and marking

VF verbal feedback; WS worked with support; I independent; NS next step in green; // self-edit; ? read this back to me; E actual evidence banked; R responded. R only when Voice and Audience are present, one NS is set and the pupil responds in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. Offer to the Communication portfolio; staff confirm mapping.
Book first and scope

Book/usual aids record only chosen plans and learning responses. The private My strategy that works card is the intentional fill-in exception; pupil keeps it. Its title is not a claim of guaranteed success. No names, real worries or card contents in shared evidence. Plan in any language. Only BUILD Week 6 authored; no later strand built.

Wednesday 10 February 2027 · P1 · 40 minutes · Year A
RSHE · BUILD · three to four learners · Spring 1 Week 6 · 8–12 February
Theme Resilience & Change. This is the assessing week. Six-week term; final week.
Exact outcome
Show a coping strategy in a real situation.
Learning and evidence

Choose and actually show a familiar safe strategy in up to three mild circuit contexts. No added noise, surprise switch, induced frustration or real-worry account. Record actual action/request separately from card choice and explanation. Fewer stations, pass and observer route are valid. Pupil keeps the strategy card; it is not collected evidence.
Forty minutes
Assessing week record

Use the six verbatim outcomes and unticked Shown / With help / Not seen grid. Cite dated evidence, context, action and support. Do not infer all six from one try. Week 3 requires actual unprompted calming use with usual aids. Week 6 real-situation use stays Not seen unless a safe natural event or specific dated prior record shows it. Circuit simulation alone does not meet that element.
Access and private help

Every task keeps bank, starter and model; usual aids remain. Log content cues separately. Actual physical action cannot be scribed. Own Yes/A bit/No/Not sure is valid. Support privately without pressing; any disclosure goes to the safeguarding lead through school procedure. No probing or secrecy promise.
